meta.title: The Practice — Dr Robert Freudenthal
meta.description: Areas of instruction by subject matter: eating disorder psychiatry, general adult and older adult psychiatry, and medical emergencies in eating disorders.

sections.label: The Practice
sections.quote: Two clinical populations. <t>One legal question, approached from opposite ends.</t>
body: Eating disorder psychiatry and dual accreditation in adult and older adult psychiatry put the same question in front of a clinician from two directions: when does a person retain the capacity to refuse treatment, and what should follow when they do not.
That is the question a Court of Protection case turns on. His 2026 paper on the role of palliative care in the treatment of anorexia nervosa takes on the hardest version of it.

sections.label: Areas of instruction
sections.title: By subject matter, <t>not by case.</t>
sections.intro: The areas below reflect clinical experience declared on his Expert Witness Institute profile. No case, no clinical detail and no outcome appears anywhere on this page — and instruction volume, court attendance and fees are matters to establish directly, not to advertise.

rows.d: Consultant practice at St Ann's Eating Disorder Service since 2022. Executive Committee of the Faculty of Eating Disorders at the Royal College of Psychiatrists since 2023. Mentor on the College's eating disorder credential since 2025.
Higher training in North Central London, 2017–2022, following core psychiatry training in the same deanery, 2014–2017.
The second half of a dual higher training, completed 2022. The capacity question arrives here from the opposite direction to eating disorders, and is no easier.
MEED training delivered to mental health Trusts, acute Trusts and medical students since 2022. Peer reviewer for the Quality Network for Eating Disorders since 2024.
